Acidity and A mphoterism of C omplex I ons

When dissolved in water, many metal ions increase the acidity of the solution. The iron(III) ion is an example: Each dissolved Fe31 ion is strongly solvated by six water mol­e­cules, leading to a complex ion Fe(H O) 2 6 31. This complex ion can act as a Brønsted–Lowry acid, donating hydrogen ions to the solvent, water:
